builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: TradeWar: A Benchmark for Execution-Grounded Trade Negotiation with Adaptive LLM Agents
summary: The method replaces static prompting and memory-only negotiation agents with an agent that consolidates prior experience, models opponents, and adapts strategy across episodes using execution-grounded settlement outcomes, without updating base LLM weights. The cost is a purpose-built simulation environment (TradeWar) with capacity and network constraints, multi-episode orchestration, and iterative strategy refinement infrastructure, all of which require substantial domain-specific engineering beyond standard LLM deployment. It can fail if the settlement model does not reflect real-world trade dynamics, if cross-episode adaptation overfits to simulation artifacts, or if the Economic Health Index misaligns with actual production objectives, and the approach has not been validated outside this benchmark.
rationale: This is a research benchmark with a tightly coupled simulation environment and evaluation metric; the adaptation technique is inseparable from the TradeWar testbed and has no demonstrated transfer to production negotiation or decision-making tasks accessible under constrained infrastructure.
technique: Cross-episode adaptive negotiation via settlement-grounded feedback

TACTIC improves final EHI from 58.2 to 73.2 across 20 sequential episodes and three seeds, compared with 65.2 for an ablation without cross-episode updates, and attains 68.8 final EHI versus 57.1 for a zero-shot CoT baseline (PromptLLM) despite the latter's 75% agreement rate.
